docs.title: VULCANUS
docs.text: Vulcanus ingests data from Nauvis and Fulgora into a DuckDB database, enabling citation and retraction analysis.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: Vulcanus is a batch worker that reads output files from Nauvis and Fulgora (stored as JSON or Parquet) and ingests them into a DuckDB database. After ingestion it can optionally run ROR matching against nauvis records and retraction matching between nauvis and retractionwatch records.

docs.title: Key Functionalities
docs.text:
• Batch Ingestion: Reads Nauvis output files from a JSON or Parquet store and ingests them into a single nauvis table in DuckDB.
  • Fulgora Ingestion: Reads output files from each Fulgora source (e.g. ror, retractionwatch) and ingests them into separate tables per source.
  • Provider Isolation: Nauvis DOI records land in a single nauvis table; each Fulgora source gets its own table.
  • JSON Parquet Support: When the -parquet flag is given, Vulcanus reads Parquet files via DuckDB's read_parquet() function, converting columns back to JSON via to_json(row(*)) to preserve the existing table schema.
  • Faithful Preservation: Ingests raw JSON records verbatim into a JSON column in DuckDB — one row per record.
  • Retraction Matching: Optional -match-retractions flag rebuilds the retractions view, which pairs each Nauvis record with its retractionwatch notice on the paper's DOI.
  • Bidirectional Retraction Provenance: Derives both passive (X is-retracted-by Y) and active (Y retracts X) provenance strings in the retraction_provenance view.
  • ROR Matching: Optional -match-ror flag runs ROR entity matching against nauvis records, finding matching funder and affiliation organizations.
  • Table Reset: Each run empties the target tables before re-inserting, so re-running replaces the previous snapshot rather than accumulating duplicates.

docs.title: Running Vulcanus
docs.text:
go run . \
  [-only all|nauvis|fulgora|match] \
  [-nauvis-db nauvis.sqlite3] \
  [-nauvis-dir /path/to/nauvis] \
  [-fulgora-db fulgora.sqlite3] \
  [-fulgora-dir /path/to/fulgora] \
  [-duckdb vulcanus.duckdb] \
  [-parquet] \
  [-match-retractions] \
  [-match-ror]
flag default meaning -only all Which provider to ingest: nauvis, fulgora, all, or match (to only run matching without ingestion) -nauvis-db nauvis.sqlite3 Path to the nauvis SQLite database -nauvis-dir (required when -only includes nauvis) Path to the nauvis system directory (data root) -fulgora-db fulgora.sqlite3 Path to the fulgora SQLite database -fulgora-dir (required when -only includes fulgora) Path to the fulgora data root (output dir) -duckdb vulcanus.duckdb DuckDB database file to write -parquet false Read Parquet files instead of JSON -match-retractions false Run retractionwatch matching (rebuild the retraction views) after ingestion -match-ror false Run ROR matching after ingestion

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
Ingest all sources with JSON files:

go run . -nauvis-dir /data/nauvis -fulgora-dir /data/fulgora -duckdb vulcanus.duckdb

Ingest with Parquet files and run all matching:

go run . -nauvis-dir /data/nauvis -fulgora-dir /data/fulgora -duckdb vulcanus.duckdb -parquet -match-retractions -match-ror
vulcanus: ingested 1234567 nauvis records into vulcanus.duckdb
vulcanus: ingested 45678 fulgora records into vulcanus.duckdb
vulcanus: retraction matching complete
vulcanus: ROR matching complete

Run matching only (no ingestion):

go run . -only match -duckdb vulcanus.duckdb -match-retractions -match-ror
vulcanus: retraction matching complete
vulcanus: ROR matching complete

docs.title: How it works
docs.text: See How Vulcanus Works for a detailed explanation of the ingestion flow, DuckDB tables, and views.

docs.title: Deployment
docs.text:
Vulcanus is designed for batch execution. It runs to completion and exits:

  1. Parse flags and open stores
  2. Ingest Nauvis files (JSON or Parquet) into DuckDB nauvis table
  3. Ingest Fulgora files (JSON or Parquet) into DuckDB <source> tables
  4. If -match-retractions: rebuild retraction views
  5. If -match-ror: run ROR matching and write results
  6. Exit

docs.title: Dependencies
docs.text:
Nauvis and Fulgora must be run first to produce output files and update their SQLite registries:

# Nauvis: ingest and produce JSON/Parquet output
go run github.com/nexus/nauvis ingest -in /data/crossref -out /data/nauvis/out -parquet-dir /data/nauvis/parquet

# Fulgora: collect and produce JSON/Parquet output
go run github.com/nexus/fulgora collect -root /data/fulgora -parquet-dir /data/fulgora/parquet

Then Vulcanus can read the output:

go run . -nauvis-dir /data/nauvis -fulgora-dir /data/fulgora -duckdb vulcanus.duckdb -parquet

docs.title: How Vulcanus Works
docs.text: This page explains how Vulcanus operates, from the Nauvis and Fulgora data stores to the DuckDB database it maintains. It is a companion to the Overview; see there for what Vulcanus is and what it aims to.

docs.title: At a glance
docs.text:
Vulcanus is a batch worker. Nauvis and Fulgora each write output files (NDJSON or Parquet) and maintain a SQLite registry of what they have produced. Vulcanus reads those registries, locates the output files, and ingests them into DuckDB:

Nauvis SQLite ──read──▶  Nauvis output files (.json or .parquet)  ──ingest──▶  DuckDB `nauvis` table
Fulgora SQLite ──read──▶  Fulgora output files (.json or .parquet)  ──ingest──▶  DuckDB `<source>` tables

The two providers stay separate: Nauvis lands in a single nauvis table, while each Fulgora source (e.g. ror, retractionwatch) gets its own table. They can be ingested independently and re-running replaces the previous snapshot.

After the source tables exist, Vulcanus can build two derived views on top of the Nauvis and retractionwatch tables:

  • retractions — pairs each Nauvis record with its matching retractionwatch notice on the paper's DOI (nauvis.DOI = retractionwatch.OriginalPaperDOI), exposing both full records plus the matching DOI.
  • retraction_provenance — reduces matches to two consumer-ready provenance strings per match: one passive (X is-retracted-by Y) and one active (Y retracts X).

The views are only built when the -match-retractions flag is given and are a projection over the loaded tables — they never copy data.

The ROR matching (-match-ror) extracts DOI, funder names, and affiliation names from the nauvis records, matches them against the ROR database in DuckDB using a parallel worker pool, and writes results to ror_funder_matches and ror_affiliation_matches tables.

This is not transformation: Vulcanus never parses or normalises the payload. It only preserves it, one record at a time, in a single column of JSON text. Every record a provider saw is ingested; nothing is filtered away.

docs.title: The stages
docs.text: The pipeline is split into three packages and one entry point, each with one job.

docs.title: 1. Store readers — internal/nauvis and internal/fulgora
docs.text:
The store packages read from the SQLite databases that Nauvis and Fulgora maintain.

Nauvis store (internal/nauvis/store.go): - Open(path) opens the Nauvis SQLite database and returns a *Store. - Nauvis() returns every output file recorded with its DOI count. - ParquetFiles() returns the same files but with .json replaced by .parquet in the path, enabling parquet-based ingestion. - ByDOI(ctx, doi) returns the file that recorded a specific DOI.

Fulgora store (internal/fulgora/store.go): - Open(path, root) opens the Fulgora SQLite database. root is the data root under which the registry's output paths live. - Sources(ctx) returns, for every source Fulgora has collected, the latest version recorded and where its output file lives. - Source.OutputPath() joins root and the stored path to locate the JSON file. - Source.ParquetPath() derives the Parquet path by appending .parquet to the JSON path (removing .json first).

docs.title: 2. Ingest — internal/ingest
docs.text:
The ingest package loads files into DuckDB using the database/sql interface over the duckdb-go driver.

Run(ctx, src, outDir, outDB, useParquet, lg) accepts either a *nauvis.Store or a *fulgora.Store and routes to the appropriate ingestion function:

func Run(ctx context.Context, src any, outDir, outDB string, useParquet bool, lg *slog.Logger) (int, error) {
    if vis, ok := src.(*nauvis.Store); ok {
        return runNauvis(ctx, vis, outDir, outDB, useParquet, lg)
    }
    if store, ok := src.(*fulgora.Store); ok {
        return runFulgora(ctx, store, outDir, outDB, useParquet, lg)
    }
    return 0, fmt.Errorf("unknown source type %T", src)
}

docs.title: JSON ingestion (ingestFile)
docs.text:
For JSON files, ingestFile reads line by line:

  1. Open the file as an NDJSON stream (one JSON object per line).
  2. Validate each line with json.Valid().
  3. Bind each line as a parameter to INSERT INTO <table> (record) VALUES (?).
  4. Count and return the total rows inserted.

This approach processes records one at a time, using a prepared statement for efficiency.

docs.title: Parquet ingestion (ingestParquet)
docs.text:
For Parquet files, ingestParquet uses DuckDB's native read_parquet() function:

INSERT INTO nauvis (record)
SELECT to_json(row(*)) FROM read_parquet('path/to/file.parquet')

The query: 1. Reads all rows from the Parquet file via read_parquet(). 2. Converts each row to a JSON string via to_json(row(*)), preserving the existing record JSON column schema. 3. Inserts all rows in a single bulk operation.

This leverages DuckDB's columnar read capabilities — no Go-side parsing, no line-by-line iteration. The Parquet files have typed columns (31 columns for Nauvis: DOI, title, author_name[], funder_name[], etc.) that are efficiently read and serialized to JSON.

docs.title: Table management
docs.text:
ensureTable(ctx, tx, name) creates a table with a single record JSON column if it does not exist. resetTable(ctx, tx, name) calls ensureTable and then DELETE FROM <table> so re-running a provider replaces its previous snapshot.

Both use quoted(name) to safely embed table names in SQL — wrapping in double quotes and escaping embedded quotes.

docs.title: Retraction matching (RunRetractionMatches)
docs.text:
When -match-retractions is set, Vulcanus rebuilds two views:

retractions view — joins Nauvis against retractionwatch on DOI:

CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW retractions AS
SELECT
    n.record AS nauvis_record,
    r.record AS retractionwatch_record,
    json_extract_string(n.record, '$.DOI') AS matched_doi
FROM nauvis AS n
JOIN retractionwatch AS r
  ON json_extract_string(n.record, '$.DOI') =
     json_extract_string(r.record, '$.OriginalPaperDOI')

retraction_provenance view — produces bidirectional provenance strings:

CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW retraction_provenance AS
SELECT
    n.record AS nauvis_record,
    r.record AS retractionwatch_record,
    json_extract_string(n.record, '$.DOI') AS paper_doi,
    json_extract_string(r.record, '$.RetractionDOI') AS retraction_doi,
    json_extract_string(n.record, '$.DOI') || ' is-retracted-by ' || json_extract_string(r.record, '$.RetractionDOI') AS provenance
FROM nauvis AS n
JOIN retractionwatch AS r
  ON json_extract_string(n.record, '$.DOI') =
     json_extract_string(r.record, '$.OriginalPaperDOI')

UNION ALL

SELECT
    r.record AS nauvis_record,
    n.record AS retractionwatch_record,
    json_extract_string(r.record, '$.RetractionDOI') AS paper_doi,
    json_extract_string(n.record, '$.DOI') AS retraction_doi,
    json_extract_string(r.record, '$.RetractionDOI') || ' retracts ' || json_extract_string(n.record, '$.DOI') AS provenance
FROM retractionwatch AS r
JOIN nauvis AS n
  ON json_extract_string(n.record, '$.DOI') =
     json_extract_string(r.record, '$.OriginalPaperDOI')

Both views are a no-op if either nauvis or retractionwatch table is absent, so providers can be ingested at different times.

docs.title: ROR matching (RunRORMatches)
docs.text:
When -match-ror is set, Vulcanus:

  1. Queries all nauvis records, extracting DOI, funder names, and affiliation names from the record JSON column using DuckDB's json_extract_string() function.
  2. Collects unique funder and affiliation names across all papers.
  3. Matches each unique name against the ROR database using a parallel worker pool (up to 8 workers). Each worker runs MatchFunder() or MatchAffiliation() against the DuckDB ROR table.
  4. Writes results to ror_funder_matches and ror_affiliation_matches tables with columns: paper_doi, name, ror_id, ror_name, confidence.

The matching tables are reset (dropped and recreated) before each run so the results are idempotent.

docs.title: 4. Entry point — main.go
docs.text:
main.go orchestrates the batch workflow:

-nauvis-db      Nauvis SQLite database path (default nauvis.sqlite3)
-nauvis-dir     Nauvis data root directory (required to ingest nauvis data)
-fulgora-db     Fulgora SQLite database path (default fulgora.sqlite3)
-fulgora-dir    Fulgora data root directory (required to ingest fulgora data)
-duckdb         DuckDB file to write (default vulcanus.duckdb)
-only           Which to run: nauvis, fulgora, all, or match (default all)
-parquet        Read Parquet files instead of JSON (default false)
-match-ror      Run ROR matching after ingestion (default false)
-match-retractions Run retraction matching after ingestion (default false)

Flow: 1. Parse flags. If -only is "all" and matching flags are set, switch to "match" mode. 2. Validate required flags: -nauvis-dir and/or -fulgora-dir depending on -only. 3. Create an slog logger that writes to stderr. 4. If -only includes nauvis: open the Nauvis store, ingest files into DuckDB. 5. If -only includes fulgora: open the Fulgora store, ingest files into DuckDB. 6. If -match-retractions: rebuild the retractions and retraction_provenance views. 7. If -match-ror: run ROR matching against nauvis records. 8. Exit.

docs.title: The database
docs.text:
Every source table has a single column and is loaded identically — one row per record, the raw JSON document preserved as-is:

table column type notes nauvis (Nauvis) record JSON one row per Crossref work; the raw document as Nauvis wrote it <source> (Fulgora, one per source) record JSON e.g. ror, retractionwatch; same shape as nauvis, but each source has its own table

When ingesting via Parquet (-parquet), the source files have 31 typed columns for Nauvis (DOI, title, author_name[], funder_name[], etc.) and source-specific schemas for Fulgora (e.g. ROR organizations with ror_id, name, type, country, etc.). DuckDB's read_parquet() efficiently reads these columns, and to_json(row(*)) converts each row back to a JSON string that matches the existing record JSON column schema.

In addition, retraction matching (-match-retractions) derives two views that sit on the same Nauvis↔retractionwatch JOIN:

view columns type notes retractions nauvis_record JSON the full Nauvis record (Crossref item) retractionwatch_record JSON the full retractionwatch record matched_doi VARCHAR the DOI that linked the two (Nauvis's DOI) retraction_provenance nauvis_record JSON the Nauvis record for the passive row; swapped for the active row retractionwatch_record JSON the retractionwatch record for the passive row; swapped for the active row paper_doi VARCHAR Nauvis's DOI in the passive row; retraction notices' RetractionDOI in the active. Equals the join key in the passive row. retraction_doi VARCHAR Retraction notice's own DOI (RetractionDOI) in the passive row; Nauvis's DOI in the active. provenance VARCHAR bidirectional provenance: X is-retracted-by Y and Y retracts X per match, two rows per join result

The ROR matching tables (-match-ror) hold structured match results:

table columns type notes ror_funder_matches paper_doi, name, ror_id, ror_name, confidence TEXT, TEXT, TEXT, TEXT, DOUBLE Paper-to-funder ROR matches ror_affiliation_matches paper_doi, name, ror_id, ror_name, confidence TEXT, TEXT, TEXT, TEXT, DOUBLE Paper-to-affiliation ROR matches

Nauvis and Fulgora are kept separate: Nauvis always lands in the single nauvis table, while each Fulgora source gets its own table named after the source. A row in any table is a full JSON object from that provider's output — one record per input record. Because the column is declared JSON, DuckDB's JSON functions (JSON_SCHEMA, JSON_EXTRACT, ...) are available directly against the stored text once the load has happened.

Each run replaces the data: resetTable empties the target tables before re-inserting, so re-running a provider produces a clean snapshot without accumulating duplicates.

docs.title: Running Vulcanus
docs.text:
go run . [-only all|nauvis|fulgora|match] [-nauvis-dir path] [-fulgora-dir path] [-duckdb vulcanus.duckdb] [-parquet] [-match-retractions] [-match-ror]
flag default meaning -only all Which provider to ingest: nauvis, fulgora, all, or match -nauvis-db nauvis.sqlite3 Nauvis SQLite database path -nauvis-dir (required for nauvis) Nauvis data root (output dir) -fulgora-db fulgora.sqlite3 Fulgora SQLite database path -fulgora-dir (required for fulgora) Fulgora data root (output dir) -duckdb vulcanus.duckdb DuckDB database file to write -parquet false Read Parquet files instead of JSON -match-retractions false Run retraction matching after ingestion -match-ror false Run ROR matching after ingestion

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
$ go run . -nauvis-dir /data/nauvis -fulgora-dir /data/fulgora -duckdb vulcanus.duckdb -parquet -match-retractions -match-ror
vulcanus: ingested 1234567 nauvis records into vulcanus.duckdb
vulcanus: ingested 45678 fulgora records into vulcanus.duckdb
vulcanus: retraction matching complete
vulcanus: ROR matching complete

The resulting vulcanus.duckdb holds source tables, matching views, and match tables. List them with the DuckDB CLI:

$ duckdb vulcanus.duckdb
duckdb> .tables
nauvis            retractionwatch  ror
retractions       retraction_provenance
ror_funder_matches ror_affiliation_matches

The key contract is faithfulness: Vulcanus treats the bytes coming from each provider's output file as the data, and DuckDB as the place to store them for later analysis. The -parquet flag improves ingestion throughput by leveraging DuckDB's native Parquet reader instead of line-by-line JSON parsing.

docs.title: Parquet ingestion
docs.text:
When the -parquet flag is given, Vulcanus reads Parquet files instead of NDJSON. The workflow:

  1. Nauvis: nauvis.ParquetFiles() queries the SQLite registry and replaces .json with .parquet in each file path. The consolidated Parquet files (produced by nauvis ingest -parquet-dir) sit alongside the JSON files in the output directory (e.g. out/0.json and out/0.json.parquet).

  2. Fulgora: Source.ParquetPath() derives the Parquet path from the JSON output path by replacing .json with .parquet (e.g. ror/output/ror-1.34.json.parquet).

  3. Ingestion: ingestParquet() executes: sql INSERT INTO nauvis (record) SELECT to_json(row(*)) FROM read_parquet('out/0.json.parquet') DuckDB reads the columnar Parquet file natively, converts all columns (including arrays like author_name, funder_name) to JSON, and inserts into the existing record JSON column.

This preserves the existing DuckDB schema and matching logic while benefitting from Parquet's efficient columnar I/O. The Parquet files are produced by Nauvis and Fulgora when their -parquet-dir flag is set during the data collection phase.

docs.title: Design notes
docs.text:
• Batch ingestion over streaming. Vulcanus reads all files from the provider's SQLite registry in a single run, rather than consuming messages one at a time. This is simpler to reason about and avoids the complexity of distributed queues.

  • Round-trip preservation over transformation. The ingest step preserves bytes, not parse results. For JSON, records are bound verbatim into the JSON column. For Parquet, columns are converted back to JSON via to_json(row(*)).

  • Replace-on-reload. Tables are emptied before each ingestion, so re-running a provider produces a clean snapshot. This avoids duplicate records and simplifies matching — views and match tables are always consistent with the current data.

  • Separate tables per provider. Nauvis is the "main" data in nauvis; Fulgora sources are enrichment data, each in its own table. Keeping them separate preserves that distinction and lets either be ingested independently.

  • Matching is optional and additive. ROR and retraction matching are opt-in via flags. Without them, Vulcanus only populates the source tables. With them, it adds views and match tables on top of the source data.

docs.title: Bidirectional Retraction Provenance (Spec)
docs.text: Status: Implemented — a UNION ALL active-direction query was added to the existing retraction_provenance view, and tests from §6 were committed alongside the existing provenance tests.

docs.title: 1. Context
docs.text:
The current retraction_provenance view produces one direction of the relationship between a Nauvis record and its matching retractionwatch notice:

<NAUVIS_DOI> is-retracted-by <RETRACTION_DOI>

This asserts the passive direction — which paper is being retracted, and by which notice. It reads well from the perspective of someone querying a database for "what retract this DOI".

docs.title: 2. Purpose
docs.text:
Add the active direction as a second entry per match:

<RETRACTION_DOI> retracts <NAUVIS_DOI>

This reads naturally from the retraction notice's perspective — which paper does * this* retract? Both directions coexist in the existing retraction_provenance view.

docs.title: 3.1 SQL
docs.text:
The view adds a UNION ALL sub-query for the active direction alongside the existing passive direction, both projecting the same five columns:

CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW retraction_provenance AS
    SELECT
        n.record AS nauvis_record,
        r.record AS retractionwatch_record,
        json_extract_string(n.record, '$.DOI') AS paper_doi,
        json_extract_string(r.record, '$.RetractionDOI') AS retraction_doi,
        json_extract_string(n.record, '$.DOI')
            || ' is-retracted-by '
            || json_extract_string(r.record, '$.RetractionDOI') AS provenance
    FROM nauvis AS n
    JOIN retractionwatch AS r
      ON json_extract_string(n.record, '$.DOI') =
         json_extract_string(r.record, '$.OriginalPaperDOI')

UNION ALL

    SELECT
        r.record AS nauvis_record,
        n.record AS retractionwatch_record,
        json_extract_string(r.record, '$.RetractionDOI') AS paper_doi,
        json_extract_string(n.record, '$.DOI') AS retraction_doi,
        json_extract_string(r.record, '$.RetractionDOI')
            || ' retracts '
            || json_extract_string(n.record, '$.DOI') AS provenance
    FROM retractionwatch AS r
    JOIN nauvis AS n
      ON json_extract_string(n.record, '$.DOI') =
         json_extract_string(r.record, '$.OriginalPaperDOI')

docs.title: 3.2 Rows per match
docs.text:
Each Nauvis↔retractionwatch join key X = Y yields two rows:

# provenance column 1 X is-retracted-by Y 2 Y retracts X

The row order is not guaranteed across DuckDB implementations — consumers should not depend on sort order. Both rows share the same (paper_doi, retraction_doi) pair but in swapped column assignments for the active reading, and neither *_record column reflects the other's perspective (they keep their original side: nauvis_record always holds the Nauvis record JSON as ingested, retractionwatch_record always holds the retractionwatch record JSON).

docs.title: 3.3 Column semantics after this spec
docs.text:
column type values for row 1 values for row 2 nauvis_record JSON Nauvis record retractionwatch record (swapped) retractionwatch_record JSON retractionwatch record Nauvis record (swapped) paper_doi VARCHAR nauvis.DOI retractionwatch.RetractionDOI retraction_doi VARCHAR retractionwatch.RetractionDOI nauvis.DOI provenance VARCHAR X is-retracted-by Y Y retracts X

Note. Swapping the records in row 2 means nauvis_record may hold what originated from Fulgora and vice versa. A consumer that needs to know which side a record came from should query the retractions view instead, or filter by checking whether paper_doi was originally from Nauvis (using the existing (paper_doi, retraction_doi) pair consistency constraint with retractions).

docs.title: 4.1 Join key
docs.text: Identical to the existing view: a row is produced when the Nauvis record's DOI equals the retractionwatch record's OriginalPaperDOI. No new matching logic.

docs.title: 4.2 Row count per match
docs.text: Exactly two rows are produced per join result — one passive, one active. The previous single-row-per-match behaviour is replaced; row counts for this view will double after migration.

docs.title: 4.3 String format
docs.text:
direction format example passive (existing) <paper_doi> is-retracted-by <retraction_doi> 10.1/paper is-retracted-by 10.1/retract active (new) <retraction_doi> retracts <paper_doi> 10.1/retract retracts 10.1/paper

No trailing whitespace, no surrounding quotes for either string.

docs.title: 4.4 Availability
docs.text: The view becomes queryable the moment both nauvis and retractionwatch tables exist — identical to the existing behaviour. If either table is missing it is a no-op (the view is absent).

docs.title: 4.5 Rebuild on every ingest
docs.text: CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW means each successful ingest re-derives the view from current table contents, so it is always in sync. Both directions are built or absent together — neither is partially present.

docs.title: 4.6 Idempotent across re-runs
docs.text: Re-running a provider clears only its own tables and rebuilds the view; no duplicate rows accumulate per direction. Each (paper_doi, retraction_doi, provenance) triple is unique in the view.

docs.title: 4.7 No-op safety
docs.text: If any file fails during ingest (e.g. invalid JSON), the whole transaction rolls back and the prior view is left intact.

docs.title: 5. Cross-view consistency
docs.text: The (paper_doi, retraction_doi) pairs produced by both directions are identical. If a consumer sees a pair in one row but not the other after an ingest, something has drifted — the existing retractions view remains the ground truth for which pairs exist.

docs.title: 6. Verification (proposed tests)
docs.text: All tests live in internal/ingest/, reuse the existing helpers (openStore, openFulgoraStoreWithLines, freshDB, countRows, quoted, viewExists), and query the view through a plain SELECT.

docs.title: 6.1 TestRetractionProvenance_Bidirectional_BothDirectionsPresent
docs.text:
Seed one Nauvis row ("DOI":"10.1/paper") matched by a retractionwatch row ("OriginalPaperDOI":"10.1/paper","RetractionDOI":"10.1/rc"). Assert the view contains two rows:

  • provenance = "10.1/paper is-retracted-by 10.1/rc"
  • provenance = "10.1/rc retracts 10.1/paper"

docs.title: 6.2 TestRetractionProvenance_Bidirectional_ColumnValues
docs.text:
After seeding one match, assert for each row:

  • Passive row: paper_doi = nauvis.DOI, retraction_doi = retractionwatch.RetractionDOI
  • Active row: paper_doi = retractionwatch.RetractionDOI, retraction_doi = nauvis.DOI

docs.title: 6.3 TestRetractionProvenance_TwoRowsPerMatch
docs.text: One Nauvis DOI matched by one retraction notice. Assert exactly two rows in the view and that there are no more — matching is not expanded or duplicated.

docs.title: 6.4 TestRetractionProvenance_MultipleNoticePairs_ExactCount
docs.text: One Nauvis DOI (10.1/paper) matched by three distinct retraction notices (10.1/rc1, 10.1/rc2, 10.1/rc3). Assert exactly six rows (3 pairs x 2 directions) and that each pair appears in both directions — no missing combinations, no extra duplicates.

docs.title: 6.5 TestRetractionProvenance_NoMatchYieldsEmptyView
docs.text: Nauvis DOI (10.1/different) matched by nothing; the view exists but has zero rows.

docs.title: 6.6 TestRetractionProvenance_IdempotentAcrossReRuns
docs.text: Re-run Nauvis and Fulgora twice each; assert the row count is exactly matches x 2 (no accumulated duplicates) and that both directions appear for each pair byte-for-byte.

docs.title: 6.7 TestRetractionProvenance_AppearsOnlyWhenBothTablesExist
docs.text: After Nauvis only, no rows. After Fulgora adds retractionwatch, all pairs appear in both directions. Mirrors the existing test for the base view.

docs.title: 6.8 TestRetractionProvenance_MatchesRetractionsView_PairsIdentical
docs.text: After ingesting Nauvis and Fulgora, assert that the set of (paper_doi, retraction_doi) pairs from the combined bidirectional rows matches exactly the pairs in the existing retractions view — same constraint as the existing test, applied to both directions together.

docs.title: 7. Migration, schema, and files
docs.text:
No schema change and no migration. The only change is the SQL of the existing retraction_provenance view (adding a UNION ALL from the retractionwatch join). The new tests live in retractions_test.go alongside existing ones.

No changes to nauvis.go, fulgora.go, ingest.go, store, or main.go.

docs.title: 8. Consistency with retractions view
docs.text: The (paper_doi, retraction_doi) set from both directions is identical to the (matched_doi, RetractionDOI) set from retractions. The two existing views share exactly one join predicate and never produce divergent pairs — the new active direction duplicates the same match in a different orientation.

docs.title: Retraction Provenance Derivation (Spec)
docs.text: Status: Spec only — proposes adding a retraction_provenance view to Vulcanus. No code has been changed; this document describes the intended data, its derivation from the existing ingest pipeline, and verification.

docs.title: 1. Purpose
docs.text:
Vulcanus currently lets a consumer answer one retraction question: "Is the retraction watch aware of a retraction for a record I hold in Nauvis?" via the derived retractions view, whose rows pair each Nauvis record with every matching retractionwatch notice on DOI = OriginalPaperDOI.

This spec proposes deriving a second, flattened, consumer-ready view that turns each Nauvis↔retractionmatch into a single string asserting provenance:

<NAUVIS_DOI> is-retracted-by <RETRACTION_DOI>

In other words, for a given Nauvis DOI that matches a Fulgora retractionwatch OriginalPaperDOI, we emit one row of the form <DOI> is-retracted-by <RetractionDOI>. This is a durable, queryable record of which retraction notice (by its own RetractionDOI) retracts which paper, as determined by Vulcanus — a provenance assertion that can be exported straight to CSV/Parquet, joined downstream, or embedded in RDF without per-row string assembly.

docs.title: 2. Location in the pipeline
docs.text:
This work adds a third derived view alongside the existing retractions view in the ingest transaction. retractions produces the joined records; this view produces provenance strings from exactly those joins. The two share the same matching key and the same availability precondition — a new author view sits on top of the same Nauvis↔retractionwatch JOIN.

Because it is a view over the already-loaded tables (a projection, not a loaded table), this follows the established pattern in docs/how-it-works.md: it is always in sync with nauvis and retractionwatch, is rebuilt on every ingest, and holds no copy of the raw bytes.

docs.title: 2.1 Where it differs from retractions
docs.text: The retractions view exposes full JSON records side by side; this spec produces a narrow, typed projection — the DOI keys plus the composed string. This is not transformation of any payload's content: no record is rewritten or pruned. The X is-retracted-by string is a derived label over two already-present JSON-extracted columns, exactly the kind of "link by key that the existing view already performs" the docs already carve out as the one allowed exception to Vulcanus's preserve-bytes rule.

docs.title: 3.1 SQL
docs.text:
CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW retraction_provenance AS
SELECT
    n.record AS nauvis_record,
    r.record AS retractionwatch_record,
    json_extract_string(n.record, '$.DOI') AS paper_doi,
    json_extract_string(r.record, '$.RetractionDOI') AS retraction_doi,
    json_extract_string(n.record, '$.DOI')
        || ' is-retracted-by '
        || json_extract_string(r.record, '$.RetractionDOI') AS provenance
FROM nauvis AS n
JOIN retractionwatch AS r
  ON json_extract_string(n.record, '$.DOI') =
     json_extract_string(r.record, '$.OriginalPaperDOI')

The provenance column holds the exact request output: <DOI> is-retracted-by <RetractionDOI>.

docs.title: 3.2 Columns
docs.text:
column type notes nauvis_record JSON the full Nauvis record (Crossref item). Retained for debugging/join context. retractionwatch_record JSON the full retractionwatch notice. paper_doi VARCHAR nauvis.DOI, the retracted paper's DOI. Equals the join key. retraction_doi VARCHAR retractionwatch.RetractionDOI, the retraction notice's own DOI. provenance VARCHAR paper_doi || ' is-retracted-by ' || retraction_doi — the requested string.

The retraction_doi and provenance columns are the primary output. The *_record columns are retained so a consumer who needs more context (title, retraction date, etc.) never has to re-join — while a consumer who only wants the string can SELECT provenance FROM retraction_provenance directly.

docs.title: 4. Behavioural contract
docs.text:
4.1 Join key. A row is produced when the Nauvis record's DOI equals the retractionwatch record's OriginalPaperDOI — identical matching to the existing retractions view. The provenance string links a Nauvis DOI to a Fulgora RetractionDOI via the requested "DOI is-retracted-by RetractionDOI" syntax.

4.2 Shape of the string. The output is paper_doi, a single space, the literal is-retracted-by, a single space, then retraction_doi. No trailing whitespace, no surrounding quotes: 10.1/yes is-retracted-by 10.1/no.

4.3 One row per match. Multiple retraction notices pointing at the same Nauvis DOI each produce their own row (one provenance string each), exactly as the retractions view does. A single retracted paper is never collapsed into one string; notices are not concatenated.

4.4 Availability. The view becomes queryable the moment both nauvis and retractionwatch tables exist, identically to retractions. If either table is missing it is a no-op (the third author view is also absent; neither retractions nor this view is partially present).

4.5 Rebuild on every ingest. CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW means each successful ingest — Nauvis or Fulgora, either provider — re-derives the view from current table contents, so it is always in sync.

4.6 Idempotent across re-runs. Re-running a provider clears only its own tables and rewrites the view idempotently; the result set never accumulates duplicate rows.

4.7 No-op safety. The third author view, like the existing ones, is rebuilt under the same single transaction as the ingest. If any file fails (e.g. invalid JSON), the whole run rolls back and the prior view is left intact, preserving the coexist safety property.

docs.title: 5. Consistency with retractions
docs.text: The two views must always agree on matches: the set of (paper_doi, retraction_doi) pairs appearing in retraction_provenance is identical to the set of (matched_doi, r.RetractionDOI) pairs in retractions. They share one JOIN predicate with the same key. When both the existing retractions view and the new view are queried against the same DuckDB, every provenance.paper_doi must appear as a retractions.matched_doi, and every provenance.retraction_doi must pair with that DOI in retractions. This constraint — that the author view's join is exactly the existing one and never a superset or subset — is the core of its behavioural contract and is what the tests in §6 pin down.

docs.title: 6. Verification (proposed tests)
docs.text:
All tests live in internal/ingest/, reuse the existing helpers (openStore, openFulgoraStoreWithLines, freshDB, viewExists, countRows, quoted), and exercise the view through a plain SELECT, exactly as TestRetractionsView_MatchesByDOI does for the existing view.

  • TestRetractionProvenance_BuildsRequestedString. Seed one Nauvis row ("DOI":"10.1/yes") matched by a retractionwatch row ("OriginalPaperDOI":"10.1/yes","RetractionDOI":"10.1/no"). Query SELECT provenance, paper_doi, retraction_doi FROM retraction_provenance and assert the single row yields provenance = "10.1/yes is-retracted-by 10.1/no", with paper_doi = "10.1/yes" and retraction_doi = "10.1/no".
  • TestRetractionProvenance_NoMatchYieldsEmptyView. Nauvis DOI (10.1/different) matched by nothing; the view exists but has zero rows.
  • TestRetractionProvenance_MultipleNotices. One Nauvis DOI (10.1/yes) matched by two retractionwatch rows with distinct RetractionDOIs (10.1/rc1, 10.1/rc2). Assert two rows with distinct provenance strings and that notices are not concatenated.
  • TestRetractionProvenance_IdempotentAcrossReRuns. Re-run Nauvis and Fulgora twice each; assert exactly one row per notice (no duplicates) and that the string is byte-for-byte stable.
  • TestRetractionProvenance_AppearsOnlyWhenBothTablesExist. After Nauvis only, the view is absent; after Fulgora follows, it appears. This mirrors TestRetractionsView_AppearsOnlyWhenBothTablesExist and guards the no-op-when- missing contract.
  • TestRetractionProvenance_MatchesRetractionsView. After ingesting Nauvis and Fulgora, assert the (paper_doi, retraction_doi) pairs in retraction_provenance are exactly the (matched_doi, retraction_doi) pairs in retractions. This pins the cross-view consistency constraint in §5 (that no new matching logic was introduced) and prevents the new view from drifting from the existing retractions join in any future change.

docs.title: 7. Migration, schema, and files
docs.text: There is no schema change: no new table or migration is added. The only new object is the retraction_provenance view, created inside the same transaction as the ingest, using existing helper routines (tablesExist, quoted). The third author view lives in retractions.go next to retractionsViewName and buildRetractionsView; it reuses the existing buildRetractionsView function (add the third view after the existing one) and its tests live in retractions_test.go alongside the existing retraction-view tests. No changes to nauvis.go, fulgora.go, ingest.go, store, or main.go are required, and the docs/how-it-works.md and index.md "The database" tables are extended to list retraction_provenance.

docs.title: Current Problem
docs.text:
All data (nauvis/Crossref works, ROR organizations, Retraction Watch records) is stored as JSON strings in a single column per table. Every query extracts fields via json_extract_string(), preventing:

  • Column-level compression
  • Predicate pushdown / vectorized scans
  • Native columnar storage benefits
  • Index usage on match-critical fields

Parquet ingestion already reads columnar files but immediately converts them back to JSON (to_json(STRUCT_PACK(...))), losing all optimization benefits.

docs.title: Target Architecture
docs.text: Keep the existing record JSON column for raw data and provenance, but add denormalized columns for fields used in matching/joins:

docs.title: nauvis table
docs.text: Column Type Indexed? Source record JSON no Full Crossref work JSON (existing) doi TEXT yes (unique) $.DOI funder_names JSON no $.funder[*].name as JSON array affiliation_names JSON no $.author[*].affiliation[*].name as JSON array

docs.title: ror table
docs.text: Column Type Indexed? Source record JSON no Full ROR organization JSON (existing) ror_id TEXT yes (unique) $.id country TEXT yes $.country status TEXT yes $.status names JSON no $.names[*].value as JSON array

docs.title: retractionwatch table (unchanged — already minimal)
docs.text: Column Type Indexed? Source record JSON no Full record (existing) original_paper_doi TEXT yes (indexed) $.original_paper_doi retraction_doi TEXT no $.retraction_doi

docs.title: Phase 1: Schema migration — add columns and populate
docs.text:
A one-time migration that transforms existing tables:

-- Add columns to existing tables
ALTER TABLE nauvis ADD COLUMN doi TEXT;
ALTER TABLE nauvis ADD COLUMN funder_names JSON;
ALTER TABLE nauvis ADD COLUMN affiliation_names JSON;

ALTER TABLE ror ADD COLUMN ror_id TEXT;
ALTER TABLE ror ADD COLUMN status TEXT;
ALTER TABLE ror ADD COLUMN names JSON;

ALTER TABLE retractionwatch ADD COLUMN original_paper_doi TEXT;
ALTER TABLE retractionwatch ADD COLUMN retraction_doi TEXT;

Populate from existing JSON:

UPDATE nauvis
SET doi = json_extract_string(record, '$.DOI'),
    funder_names = json_extract(record, '$.funder[*].name'),
    affiliation_names = json_extract(record, '$.author[*].affiliation[*].name');

UPDATE ror
SET ror_id = json_extract_string(record, '$.id'),
    status = json_extract_string(record, '$.status'),
    names = CAST(json_extract(record, '$.names[*].value') AS JSON);

UPDATE retractionwatch
SET original_paper_doi = json_extract_string(record, '$.original_paper_doi'),
    retraction_doi = json_extract_string(record, '$.retraction_doi');

Create indexes:

CREATE UNIQUE INDEX idx_nauvis_doi ON nauvis(doi);
CREATE INDEX idx_nauvis_funder ON nauvis(funder_names) USING GIN;
CREATE INDEX idx_nauvis_affil ON nauvis(affiliation_names) USING GIN;

CREATE UNIQUE INDEX idx_ror_id ON ror(ror_id);
CREATE INDEX idx_ror_country ON ror(country);
CREATE INDEX idx_ror_status ON ror(status);

CREATE INDEX idx_retraction_doi ON retractionwatch(original_paper_doi);

docs.title: Phase 2: Ingest code changes
docs.text:
Modify ingest.go ingestParquet() and ingestFile() to populate denormalized columns:

// ingestParquet with typed columns
INSERT INTO nauvis (record, doi, funder_names, affiliation_names)
SELECT
    to_json(STRUCT_PACK(...)),
    doi,
    funder_name,
    affiliation_name
FROM read_parquet(?)

For the JSON path, extract fields during INSERT:

insertStmt, err := tx.PrepareContext(ctx, `
    INSERT INTO nauvis (record, doi, funder_names, affiliation_names)
    VALUES (?,
        json_extract_string(?, '$.DOI'),
        json_extract(?, '$.funder[*].name'),
        json_extract(?, '$.author[*].affiliation[*].name')
    )
`)

Same pattern for ror and retractionwatch tables.

docs.title: ROR matching (match/duckdb.go)
docs.text:
Replace JSON extraction query with direct column access:

// Before (json_extract_string on every row)
q := `
    SELECT id, country, status, name_values
    FROM ror
    WHERE LOWER(array_to_string(json_extract_string(record, '$.names[*].value'), ',')) LIKE LOWER(?)
    LIMIT ?
`

// After (direct column scan, country/status used in WHERE clause)
q := `
    SELECT ror_id, country, status, names
    FROM ror
    WHERE LOWER(array_to_string(names::VARCHAR, ',')) LIKE LOWER(?)
      AND status <> 'withdrawn'  -- push down the exclusion
    LIMIT ?
`

With the status column indexed, DuckDB can skip withdrawn organizations entirely.

docs.title: ROR matching (match/matching.go)
docs.text:
The MatchFunder function already filters by country region. With the country column indexed, the pre-filter query becomes:

// Before: fetch all candidates then filter in Go
// After: let DuckDB pre-filter
query := `SELECT ror_id, country, names FROM ror WHERE status = 'active' AND country = ?`

This reduces candidate count dramatically before fuzzy matching.

docs.title: Retraction matching (ingest/retractions.go)
docs.text:
Replace JSON-based joins with column-based joins:

-- Before
FROM nauvis AS n
JOIN retractionwatch AS r
  ON json_extract_string(n.record, '$.doi') = json_extract_string(r.record, '$.original_paper_doi')

-- After (uses indexed TEXT columns, can use hash/nested loop join on DOI)
FROM nauvis AS n
JOIN retractionwatch AS r
  ON n.doi = r.original_paper_doi

docs.title: Phase 4: Parquet ingestion optimization
docs.text:
Instead of converting parquet columns back to JSON, store them directly into typed columns:

func ingestParquetNauvis(ctx context.Context, tx *sql.Tx, path string, lg *slog.Logger) (int, error) {
    // Direct column projection from parquet into typed table columns
    query := `
        INSERT INTO nauvis (record, doi, funder_names, affiliation_names)
        SELECT
            to_json(T),
            T.doi,
            T.funder_name,
            T.author_name
        FROM read_parquet(?) AS T
    `
    _, err := tx.ExecContext(ctx, query, path)
    return err
}

For parquet files that already have the right columns, this is a zero-copy read + select, no STRUCT_PACK round-trip.

docs.title: Performance Expectations
docs.text:
Operation Current After ROR query (LIKE match) Full table scan, JSON deserialize all rows Column scan on names column, predicate on status + country ROR matching with country filter 200 candidates per name (all active), filtered in Go Candidates pre-filtered by DuckDB Retraction join Join on extracted JSON strings Join on indexed TEXT columns Parquet ingest Read parquet → STRUCT_PACK → to_json → insert JSON string Read parquet → project columns → insert Storage size JSON text (duplicated across record column + extracted fields) Columnar parquet-like storage in DuckDB for typed columns

DuckDB stores VARCHAR columns using LZ4 compression internally, and the denormalized columns can be scanned using vectorized execution without JSON parsing overhead.

docs.title: Risk & Rollback
docs.text:
• Backward compatibility: The record JSON column is preserved byte-for-byte. Downstream consumers that rely on it continue to work.
  • Zero-downtime migration: The migration is a one-time ALTER TABLE + UPDATE that can run alongside existing data. The old query path (via JSON) still works for all tables during transition.
  • Rollback: Drop the new columns and indexes; everything reverts to the existing behavior.

docs.title: Order of Operations
docs.text:
1. Write migration SQL (Phase 1)
  2. Test migration on existing vulcanus.duckdb
  3. Update ingest.go to populate new columns (Phase 2)
  4. Update match/duckdb.go to use typed columns (Phase 3)
  5. Update match/matching.go to use country filter (Phase 3)
  6. Update ingest/retractions.go join (Phase 3)
  7. Optimize parquet ingest (Phase 4)
  8. Benchmark before/after
